I know I'm late as fuck, but I spent this past week battling with a feature for a game I've been working on. I'm essentially trying to get randomly generated islands to appear, but quite a few algorithms I've tried didn't yield a very good result. Thankfully I found a very simple solution that only requires some compromises on my part (in that the width and height of the area I'm working on must be the same size). Sometimes programming gets you down, but once you get something working... Jesus you feel like you're on top of the world!

Congratulations! Could this "width and height must be equal" be thought of like the chunks in minecraft? I know that chunks are geometric cubes composed of blocks in the game, where each block inside can have unique attributes.

That would allow for you to use the increased efficiency while maintaining the appearance of natural asymmetry.

Well essentially the world is comprised of 2D tiles. And what I'm doing is somewhat taken from Civ 5, in that essentially I'm defining a series of boundaries where continents/islands/whatever can spawn. For this to work, the boundaries need to be squares (as this was really the only thing I could get working). However, the islands basically form nice shapes, and I could have a bunch of boundaries overlap to hide the square-ness of them I figure.

Oh, duh, shouldn't have assumed 3D.

Sounds neat! If I am imagining this correctly, the squares themselves would overlap with portions of the other squares? If so, would it be possible to make a "blending" function that takes two square border objects (with xy dimensions and xy coordinates of one of the corners) as arguments, checks if they overlap, and then modifies the overlapped portions by passing through the shared area by columns and (by some algorithm) dividing it up between the two overlapping border objects? This would solve the issue of shared land, and potentially make borders prettier and less square.

That's not very efficient, but it would techincally work.

Also, you could try going the efficiency freak route and only generate the parts of the map that the player has discovered so far. Break each square block into maybe three hundred small "environment" objects (call them acres maybe?) that can be land, water, lava, etc., and give each object an id which associates that environment acre with a generated "nation" entity. The block generation for the first block of the game would start by rolling a random acre for one of the corners, and then procedurally generating all the rest by randomly deciding whether the next acre will have the same id as a neighbor (expanding that nation), no id (i.e. unowned land), or have a new id created. Then when neighboring blocks are generated, the new "edge" acres along the border of the block would reference the id of the adjacent acre in the neighboring block if it rolled to share the id of a neighbor.

I guess the block could generate acres in an inwards traveling spiral pattern. That would be cool. And it would guarantee that the neighboring block's nations could have a chance at expanding their borders well into the next block.
